title: Employ staff under the Oil Refining and Manufacturing Award 2020
what: Pay and employ staff at no less than the terms of the Oil Refining and Manufacturing Award 2020.

sources.title: Oil Refining and Manufacturing Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.1 This industry award covers employers throughout Australia in the oil refining and manufacturing industry and their employees in the classifications listed in Schedule A —Classification Definitions to the exclusion of any other modern award.

sources.title: Oil Refining and Manufacturing Award 2020
sources.quote: 4.2 Oil refining and manufacturing industry means: (a) refining crude oil; (b) manufacturing and blending petroleum products including: (i) aviation fuels; (ii) bitumen; (iii) diesel; (iv) ethylene; (v) gasoline; (vi) liquefied petroleum gas; (vii) lubricant base oils, greases and other related product lines; or (viii) solvents; and (c) pipeline distribution of oil or petroleum products included in this definition to or from a terminal or storage facility owned and operated by a refinery employer or a related company, which is itself connected by pipeline to an oil refinery, and the operation of such a terminal or storage facility; and (d) storage of bulk liquid at a bulk liquid terminal, provided that immediately prior to 1 January 2010, the employer of any employees at such terminal was bound by the Oil and Gas Industry Bulk Liquid Terminals Award 2002 [ AP822096CRV ].

sources.publisher: Government of Western Australia (Private Sector Labour Relations)
sources.quote: The state system covers: Private sector businesses and their employees that operate as: Sole traders. Partnerships, where none of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

assessment.summary: The Oil Refining and Manufacturing Award sets the industry's classifications, minimum pay, allowances and penalty rates on top of the National Employment Standards.

marks.reason: Classifications, allowances, penalty rates and their record-keeping add to the cost and complexity of employing in the industry.
